settings.heading: An heirloom sensibility
settings.text:
Pitriciacle is built on a belief older than any trend: that a home gathers meaning the way a family does — slowly, piece by piece. Our designs borrow their silhouettes from Rajput arches, Mughal jharokhas and temple brass, then pare them back for rooms that breathe.

Nothing here shouts. Everything here stays.
We begin with a single workshop partnership in Rajasthan — carved wooden mirrors inspired by palace architecture, made one frame at a time.
settings.title: The first frame

settings.text: Metalsmiths in Uttar Pradesh join the atelier. Kansa, peetal and tamba — India's ancient alloys — become serving bowls, urlis and carafes for the modern table.
settings.title: The alloys

settings.text: Weavers and lighting artisans complete the home: hand-knotted wool, handloom cotton runners, and lamps that warm a room the way candlelight does.
settings.title: The whole room

settings.author: Aisha
settings.quote: The Jharokha mirror changed our whole living room. Guests ask about it before they sit down.

settings.author: Rohan
settings.quote: You can feel the handwork in the brass — the weight, the finish. Nothing in our home gets more compliments than the urli duo.
